digest.component_or_area: LLM agent toolset management and step limiting
propositions: When tool_step_limit is enforced by filtering the toolset to empty after any tool call, pydantic-ai omits toolConfig from subsequent requests while message history contains toolUse blocks, violating Bedrock/Anthropic provider protocol constraints and raising ValidationException 400

The bounded recovery fallback in completion_recovery.py dies with the same 400 error when an evidence run reaches step 17 because the tool-hiding mechanism creates provider-invalid requests mid-protocol

Offline unit tests using FunctionModel miss the provider protocol constraint because FunctionModel accepts tools-less requests over tool_use history, leaving the real Bedrock/Anthropic constraint unrepresented

The solution replaces tool-hiding with a steering wrapper that returns a fixed notice once run_step exceeds the limit, keeping tool definitions advertised for the whole run so requests remain protocol-valid
Steering is advisory; a non-cooperative model that ignores steering and keeps issuing tool calls is still terminally bounded by the existing UsageLimits budget (request_limit and tool_calls_limit)
The steering mechanism is LIVE-proven on Bedrock us-east-1 with real agents landing cleanly after reaching the tool step limit and producing final output
